issues.label: Applicability of CCP 533 to DVRO proceedings
issues.why: The court must determine whether section 533's injunction-dissolution standard governs DVRO petitions under the DVPA.

issues.label: Authority to dismiss entire DVRO action
issues.why: Section 533 addresses modifying/dissolving injunctions, not dismissing an entire petition, raising the court's power to do so.

issues.label: Dismissal for exceeding time estimate
issues.why: Whether counsel's failure to meet a two-day estimate is a permissible basis to dismiss a DVRO petition.

issues.label: Due process right to complete evidentiary hearing
issues.why: Wife may have been denied a full and fair opportunity to present her abuse case before dismissal.

issues.label: Statutory right to hearing on merits
issues.why: DVPA entitles a petitioner to a merits determination when credible abuse allegations are presented.

issues.label: Adequacy of judicial time allocation
issues.why: Court repeatedly recognized a two-day need yet set half-day sessions, implicating its own scheduling responsibility.

issues.label: Court-conducted four-question examination sufficiency
issues.why: Whether the court's brief examination of Husband adequately supports its no-future-abuse finding.

issues.label: Standard for issuing/denying DVRO
issues.why: Whether past abuse alone suffices under the DVPA regardless of future-abuse probability.

issues.label: Evaluation of documented past abuse evidence
issues.why: The audio recording and testimony of physical abuse must be weighed under the DVPA's standard.

issues.label: Credibility determinations of Wife's allegations
issues.why: Court partly relied on non-credibility yet disclaimed insufficiency, requiring clarity on factual findings.

issues.label: Effect of Husband's voluntary promise
issues.why: Whether a respondent's promise not to abuse can justify denying protective relief.

issues.label: Dismissal without prejudice versus with prejudice
issues.why: Nature of the dismissal affects Wife's ability to refile and her protection.

issues.label: Protection of Child as protected party
issues.why: Child's separate need for protection and best interests must be independently assessed.

issues.label: Custody and visitation order consequences
issues.why: Dissolving the DVTRO affects the prior custody grant and DVPA custody presumptions.

issues.label: DVPA custody presumption under Family Code 3044
issues.why: A finding of domestic violence triggers a rebuttable presumption against the perpetrator's custody.

issues.label: Improper penalizing party for counsel conduct
issues.why: Dismissing based on attorneys' scheduling and reporter failures may unfairly punish the litigant.

issues.label: Court reporter absence attribution
issues.why: The misunderstanding over reporting services was used to justify dismissal, requiring assessment of fault.

issues.label: Reliance on CWS non-substantiation finding
issues.why: Weight to give the unsubstantiated child-abuse report despite Wife's testimony she lied under coercion.

issues.label: Relevance of non-prosecution of incidents
issues.why: Whether absence of criminal charges is a proper factor against granting civil DVRO relief.

issues.label: Consideration of coercive control evidence
issues.why: DVPA includes coercive control; financial and freedom restrictions must be evaluated as abuse.

issues.label: Immigration-status threats as abuse
issues.why: Threats of deportation may constitute coercive control or abuse under the DVPA.

issues.label: Interpretation of Igbo-language audio recording
issues.why: Reliability and translation of the bilingual recording bear on evidentiary weight.

issues.label: Whether ends-of-justice findings are supported
issues.why: The court's interest-of-justice rationale must be reviewed for adequate factual basis.

issues.label: Continuances' impact on DVTRO duration
issues.why: Multiple continuances extended restraints, factored by the court as prejudice to Husband.

issues.label: Standard of review for dismissal
issues.why: Reviewing court must identify whether abuse of discretion, de novo, or substantial evidence applies.
